Test Description: Verifies GPIO CSRs for default reset values and masked write/read behavior using defined read/write masks and default values across per-pin and group registers.
Remarks: Default-value comparison masks out bit 0 (0xfffffffe). Some registers are skipped via skip_array and skip_rst_array; VRRW registers are not written. Registers with zero read/write masks are skipped for that operation.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) For each register in [GPIO_8..GPIO_39, G9_intr_raw_stclr, INTR1_INTR_EN1, INTR1_INTR_STS1, INTR2_INTR_EN1, INTR2_INTR_STS1, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4, GPIO_DOUT_GROUP1..4, GPIO_DIN_GROUP1..4], read the value if readable and compare the value with the documented reset value after masking out bit 0; skip entries marked to skip reset check or that are not readable. 2) For each write pattern in [0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000], write the pattern masked by each register’s write mask to every writable register not marked to skip. 3) Read back each register that is both writable and readable and compare the masked read value against the expected value computed from the write-mask and the default value; report any mismatch. 4) The test passes only if all default checks and all write/read comparisons succeed with no failures.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: 1) Default value phase: For each readable, non-skipped register, the read value masked with 0xfffffffe must equal the documented reset value; any mismatch is a failure. 2) Write/read phase: For each pattern and each writable/readable, non-skipped register, the masked read value must equal the expected value derived from the write-mask and reset value; any mismatch is a failure. 3) The test passes if and only if there are zero default-value failures and zero write/read failures; otherwise it fails.

Test Description: Tests negative edge interrupts on GPIO pins 8–39 using per-pin configuration and verifies raw and group status handling via ISR.
Remarks: Timeout is bounded (5000) with a note to adjust to simulation time base. The pending flag is set before generating the edge to avoid a race.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the platform interrupt ID for the selected GPIO instance. 2) In INTR_EN1, enable the system interrupt output for the selected GPIO instance. 3) Drive the pad control register at 0xA0243ffc high to establish a known level. 4) For GPIO_8 through GPIO_39, set input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and clear raw status using the per-pin register. 5) For each bit 0..31, clear the corresponding raw bit in G9_intr_raw_stclr and enable only that bit in INTR1_INTR_EN1. 6) Arm the pending flag, then generate a falling edge on the selected pin using 0xA0243ffc (1→0). 7) Wait until the interrupt clears the pending flag or until the timeout expires; on timeout, record an error. 8) In the ISR: read the per-pin register, require DIN to be 0, require the raw status bit to be set, require the group status in INTR1_INTR_STS1 to have the bit set, then clear the per-pin raw bit and the group raw bit in G9_intr_raw_stclr. 9) Verify INTR1_INTR_STS1 is 0, clear RAW_STCR1 for the selected instance, and clear the platform interrupt.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: 1) For each pin, the pending flag must clear before timeout; otherwise it is a failure. 2) In the ISR, DIN must be 0 after a falling edge; if not, it is a failure. 3) The per-pin raw status and the corresponding bit in INTR1_INTR_STS1 must be set on entry to the ISR; if not, it is a failure. 4) After clearing, INTR1_INTR_STS1 must read 0; if not, it is a failure. 5) The test passes if no failures are recorded and finish(0) is issued.

Remarks: A bounded timeout (2000) is used to prevent infinite waits. Group interrupt enable is masked during service and re-enabled afterward.
